chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Allah, bless my community in the thard and the thareed.' Ja'far said: 'The thard is what is small, and the thareed is what is big.'
ai.seo_question: What are thard and thareed in the hadith of the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s (saww) specific supplication for blessings in thard (small bread) and thareed (bread soaked in broth), which Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (as) clarifies as referring to the size of the bread pieces. This narration underscores the cultural and spiritual significance of simple, communal meals in early Islamic society, reflecting a tradition of humility and gratitude for basic sustenance. It also illustrates the role of the Ahl al-Bayt in preserving and explaining the practical nuances of the Prophet’s sayings.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ash’ary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Prophetsaww said: ‘O Allahazwj! Bless for mysaww community regarding Al-Sard and Al-Sareyd’. Ja’far (the narrator) said, ‘Al-Sard is what is small, and Al-Sareyd is what is big’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad al-Ash‘ariy from ibn al-Qaddah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘O Lord, bless for my followers al-Thard and al-Tharid.’
Ja‘far has said, that al-Thard is whatever is small and al-Tharid is whatever is large.”
